rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 22 line 315 'A reader who internalises these six has most of the training in muscle' — 'these six' resolves against chunk 0 line 7 ('plus six recurring three-move combinations at the end'), a chunk-0 lede count reused later, the explicit NOT-violation carve-out. Second candidate: chunk 10 line 157 'One of them is psychology dressed as mechanics, which is why it sits here rather than under interaction' — the antecedent 'them' resolves cleanly in-sentence to 'Six operational moves' (line 155-156); WHICH single move earns the 'psychology' label is left for the reader to infer, but rule 1 tests antecedent resolution, not disambiguation among named alternatives, so this stays inside. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found elsewhere; every family-level 'this family' / 'them' pointer resolves to the chunk's own header noun.

No body sentence points at another file or lecture by position ('the opening lecture said'). Every example is a named prompt-registry id cited directly (e.g. chunk 24 'Example: three-minds-one-synthesis-1, three-retrievers-one-curator-1, self-consistency-after-scoreboard-1' — spot-verified this session: `find curriculum/prompts -iname 'three-minds-one-synthesis-1*'` → curriculum/prompts/three-minds-one-synthesis-1.md exists). This is a self-contained catalogue page with no narrative dependency on another file's position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -nE "you (did|saw|just|caught)|earlier module|prior module|the module you|as you saw"` over the raw file → 2 hits, both false positives on inspection: line 211 'tokens you didn't budget' (unrelated 'you'), line 297 '(*the file you just created*)' — an illustrative parenthetical inside the 'Chain back-reference' entry's own definition, describing the SHAPE of a prompt phrase, not a backward reference the page itself makes to the student's history. No genuine 'the X you did' construction present.

Checked the thinnest chunks (single-entry chunks 2, 3, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21): each still carries a full bold-lead + continuation + italic quote — e.g. chunk 15 'the critique register' (233-242) and chunk 19 'the multi-result fallback' (281-290) both close on a self-carrying claim, not a bare wait-state or context-dependent bullet.

Closest candidate: chunk 14 header 'Shape the interaction: pacing the questions' (217-232) covers two entries, 'Batched, not dumped' (pacing, direct match) and 'Push-back invitation' (disagreement tone, a looser fit). The header doesn't literally name disagreement, but nothing in the chunk CONTRADICTS 'pacing the questions' — both entries govern how/when questions land in a live exchange — which is the rule's actual bar. Every other header (e.g. 'Shape the boundary: the scope guard', 'Three-move patterns: walk-away, grill, and skill-author') is a literal, verifiable summary of its chunk's content.

`grep -nE 'Not [A-Z][a-z]+\. Not [A-Z]'` → 0 hits (no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction). `grep -nE '^Every |^each '` and manual re-read → no anaphora/epistrophe triple (line 21's three short sentences each take a DIFFERENT subject — bug, prompt, answer — not a repeated opening phrase). Self-grading-superlative sub-item, closest candidate: chunk 17 line 265 'Probably the most important clause in any prompt.' — re-read against check_writing.md §13 (`node curriculum/evals/scripts/rule.js writing 13`): §13's actual flag list is vendor/marketing-defensive framing ('not an aspirational X', 'the real practitioners', 'grounded in actual') and the rule 7 example itself is scoped to 'in the training' self-praise ('The exercise proves usefulness or nothing does'). Line 265 grades the null-case-escape MOVE's importance to prompt-craft generally, not the training's or this page's own worth — stays outside the value-prop-leak pattern. No abstraction-noun-stack or empty-leg verb-triplet found on a full re-read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `grep -n -i 'beat\|compendium\|\bmood\b\|Connections'` over the body → relevant hits: line 21 'beats wandering later' (ordinary verb), line 221 'beats the form-filling default' (ordinary verb), line 309 '*Quote the specific session beat.*' (italicised quote, per the maintainer's own 'Examples-in-the-wild... drawn from real...prompts' contract — a verbatim specimen, not authorial voice; editing it would falsify the quote the page exists to preserve). 'compendium'/'mood'/'Connections' → 0 hits in body. Chunk 2 line 39 '*The surface the skill called out harder than I would have:*' — 'surface' here reads as security-domain 'attack surface' (STRIDE/access-control context established elsewhere on the page), not the repo's meta-dialect noun ('writing surface') — different domain, ordinary usage. 'forcing function' (chunk 21 header/entry) is explicitly cleared for AE101 register by §8's own text ('ordinary shop vocabulary... unlike compendium/surface-as-noun'). No smuggled dialect found communicating in the page's own authorial voice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Every move-entry across chunks 1-21 bolds a full 1-2 sentence lead (e.g. chunk 5 line 77: '**Names a condition under which the work happens, and names refusal as a valid outcome.**', 13 words) rather than a ≲ 5-word handle. The lookup-surface carve-out turns the PER-SLIDE COUNT budget off for this reference page (1-2 bold entries per chunk, matching precedent), but its own text says 'the handle cap still binds — bold the label, not the sentence after it', and this page's format — documented in its own maintainer 'Per-entry shape' note (line 377) as deliberate: 'bold lead-in carrying both definition and the start of the why' — bolds the whole definitional clause on every one of ~30 entries. This is a house-style tension between the rule's worked example (short mode-word handles like Read:/Watch:) and a definitional-glossary shape the maintainer authored on purpose; the fix (trimming every entry to a 5-word label) would degrade the page's stated scanning function. Filed as the non-blocking TODO tier this rule occupies, not actioned — a maintainer house-style call, not a fresh defect.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Maintainer call: either add an explicit accept-note formalising the full-sentence-bold shape as this reference page's deliberate glossary format, or fold rule 9's lookup-surface carve-out to say so explicitly so future judges stop re-raising it.
